gen-fs-styro-gf-julius-sans-one: Julius Sans One spreads its letters out with wide gaps and small-looking capitals, light and unhurried. Julius Sans One keeps that pace down a whole page of plain sans text, while Styro crowds its headline tight above.
gen-fs-styro-gf-karla: Retro swagger from Styro, with letters packed nearly shut. Karla sits underneath with a gaping c and a stocky, tall middle band, so the dense heading and the open sans text give each other room to breathe.
gen-fs-styro-gf-kedebideri: Styro's letters are pressed so tight that its e and c barely show a gap. Kedebideri below is rounded, tall and open, letting the page exhale.
gen-fs-styro-gf-khula: Pressed-together letters give Styro its crowded, retro punch, with almost no opening in the e or c. Khula holds its curves wide and its midsection tall, so a long stretch of sans text feels easy to move through.
gen-fs-styro-gf-krub: Contemporary, with a hint of mischief. Styro is the one for loud, tightly packed display lines, while Krub does the quieter job of a tall plain sans, its curves left open and unfinished.
gen-fs-styro-gf-kufam: Styro comes in crowded and commanding, its retro letters pressed so close the e and c nearly seal shut. Kufam answers with tube-like, single-width strokes and generous curves.
gen-fs-styro-gf-lexend: Approachable first, then a surprise. Styro's tight, swollen-looking letters push hard at the top, and Lexend's big lowercase and open jaws, with stems and arches of identical thickness, give the sans text a steady footing.
gen-fs-styro-gf-lexend-deca: Tight, retro and loud up top, Styro crowds its letters until the e and c barely open. Lexend Deca sits under it with a plain, unshaded line and big lowercase, calming the whole page.
gen-fs-styro-gf-lexend-exa: Styro packs its retro, commanding letters so close that the e and c almost close up entirely. Lexend Exa runs wide and open, its thickness never changing, so a long page keeps an unhurried feel.
gen-fs-styro-gf-lexend-giga: Lexend Giga is flat, wide and generously tracked. Under Styro's crowded, closed-up headline, a long stretch of its plain sans text reads slowly and openly, each word given its own space.
